evidence: Cache inventory now records and rechecks the non-following directory identity. During confirmation, the Windows release path opens the exact cache directory with DELETE and read-attribute authority while denying delete sharing, then renames through SetFileInformationByHandle rather than resolving the pathname again.

After the handle-bound move, the staged tombstone must match both the confirmed root identity and full inventory before the replacement cache is created, the success audit is appended, or any bytes are deleted. Rollback uses the same held directory handle and refuses to remove or restore a substituted identity.

The project root and local .tmp staging root remain stable across the operation; cleanup verifies the exact staged root, does not follow redirects, and reports cleanup-pending if identity-safe physical removal cannot finish. Canonical project data remains outside the deletion scope and physical-erasure limitations remain explicit.

The new Windows adversarial boundary test attempts to rename the cache after confirmation while the destructive handle is held. The swap is denied, the request returns no cleared result, cached and canonical bytes remain stable, no tombstone remains, and no privacy.cache.cleared audit is recorded.

A second test replaces the cache with a junction after preview and before confirmation. Clear fails closed through project path authority, the target bytes remain unchanged, and no success audit is recorded.
The full 39-test security suite, strict contract tests, compiled desktop verifier, and 140-file quality checks pass on the exact candidate.
The strict-descendant remediation changes only the privacy cache-clear implementation and its security tests beyond the immutable R01 submission/review records and generated workflow projections.

No provider, telemetry, retention, public route, portable schema, database profile, dependency, UI reference, or unrelated capability changed. Existing privacy policy, audit-redaction, consent, session, disclosure, and approved-reference behavior remains green.

The append-only R01 review ledger remains committed and CAP-02.S04.T03-R01-F01 is replayed explicitly for independent closure; broader protected-database and full-profile work remains assigned to T04, slice review, checkpoints, and W1 exit.

verificationSelection.riskAnalysis: CAP-02.S04.T03-R01-F01 identified a high-risk destructive TOCTOU boundary capable of applying cache-deletion authority to substituted canonical data. The remediation therefore selects exact Windows handle-bound swap and redirect adversarial cases, the full local-security suite, strict privacy contracts, the complete desktop verifier, governed Python quality, unchanged approved-reference lineage, and canonical workflow integrity. Dependency scanning, SQLCipher/database protection, performance, packaging, and complete cross-capability qualification are deferred because this strict-descendant fix changes no dependencies, database engine, packaging input, UI reference, or performance contract and those surfaces belong to T04, the CAP-02.S04 slice review, checkpoints, and W1 exit.
